nodes.label: MeshTransport (Nearby wrapper)
nodes.rationale: Thin wrapper over expo-nearby-connections. Nearby gives P2P *clustering* (one-room reach) and does not relay past radio range on its own; multi-hop is delegated to utils/relay.ts, which this layer feeds and obeys. Lower device id initiates the connection so both discovering sides do not race into two half-open connections. Self-advertisements echoed back are ignored so you never appear in your own mesh. Invitations are auto-accepted because pairing already happened out of band. stopAdvertise/stopDiscovery run before start because a previous session or hot reload can leave the radio advertising and make the next start fail.

nodes.label: packName / identity smuggled in display name
nodes.rationale: Nearby only carries a display name on an advertisement, so the stable device id is packed into it as `deviceId~display` — there is no other channel for identity before a connection exists.
nodes.norm_label: packname / identity smuggled in display name

nodes.label: explain (Nearby error translation)
nodes.rationale: Nearby reports failures as a bare ApiException with a numeric status (8001-8020). Showing that mid-demo tells the user nothing, so reachable codes are translated into an action to take (retry, cycle Bluetooth, grant permission).

nodes.label: ensurePermissions (per-API-level Android grants)
nodes.rationale: Permission set varies by API level: FINE_LOCATION always, BLUETOOTH_SCAN/ADVERTISE/CONNECT from API 31, NEARBY_WIFI_DEVICES from API 33.

nodes.label: MeshTransport.broadcast (fan-out minus sender)
nodes.rationale: Sends to every connected peer except the one that handed the envelope over — the split-horizon half of loop prevention, complementing the path check in route().

nodes.label: Envelope (wire format)
nodes.rationale: Kept small because Nearby carries it as text. id survives every hop unchanged as the dedupe key; from is never rewritten by a relay; body is opaque to relays and becomes ciphertext once the vault lands; path builds the visible route strip; at is display-only and never trusted for ordering because it comes from the sender's clock.

nodes.label: route() — the whole hop rule
nodes.rationale: Pure decision function — returns drop/deliver/relay and the caller performs the side effects, so the A->B->C hop rules can be reasoned about and unit-tested with no native calls or store access. Drop order is duplicate, then loop (own id already in path), then deliver-if-mine, then TTL expiry.

nodes.label: SeenCache (bounded dedupe ring)
nodes.rationale: A plain Set would grow without bound over a long demo, so this is a fixed-size ring (512) that forgets the oldest id instead.

nodes.label: decode (tolerant JSON parse)
nodes.rationale: Never throws and shape-checks every field: a malformed payload from another build (different app version on the mesh) must not crash the app.

nodes.label: hopsTaken (path length)
nodes.rationale: 0 means it arrived directly from the sender — hops counts relays, not links, which is why UI adds one before saying "N HOPS".

nodes.label: isGroup (g: thread prefix)
nodes.rationale: Group messages are meant to be delivered to everyone AND relayed onward; declared but not yet consulted by route().

nodes.label: useMesh Zustand store (live mesh state)
nodes.rationale: Owns the transport and applies the relay rules to anything that arrives, so screens only ever read plain data. peers holds only phones reachable right now — a disconnected entry kept as a ghost node on the map reads as a bug and makes the peer count disagree with the conversation list.

nodes.label: mesh store start()
nodes.rationale: Resolves the persisted device identity before constructing the transport, so the phone you spoke to earlier is still the same phone and does not come back as a stranger. On connect it also creates a thread for an unknown peer — a phone you can reach must be a phone you can open a chat with.

nodes.label: mesh store onEnvelope handler
nodes.rationale: The side-effect executor for route()'s decision: drop increments stats, relay re-broadcasts excluding the sender, deliver upserts a message. A 'revert' kind edits an existing row to reverted rather than adding one — money that quietly disappears is worse than money you can see was returned.

nodes.label: mesh store send()
nodes.rationale: Marks its own envelope id as seen before broadcasting so the message is never relayed back to us. Message state is honest about routing: fanout 0 shows 'queued' (no peer at all means it waits, never show it as sent), directly reachable shows 'delivered', otherwise 'sent'.

nodes.label: queueCoin (cancel window)
nodes.rationale: Shows the coin in the thread immediately but holds the actual send for CANCEL_WINDOW_MS (5000) — long enough to catch a mistake, short enough not to feel broken. Deliberately one pending payment at a time: a queue of pending payments is a queue of things you cannot cancel individually under pressure.

nodes.label: revertLastCoin (post-send take-back)
nodes.rationale: Marks the original struck-through locally first so the gesture feels immediate; the peer honours the revert when the message reaches them, or when a route opens. The revert envelope carries the target message id in its body.

nodes.label: upsertMessage (thread append/create)
nodes.rationale: Creates a thread for a sender we have never heard from, so an inbound message from an unknown device id is never dropped on the floor.

nodes.label: deviceIdentity (restart-stable device id)
nodes.rationale: Without persistence every launch mints a new identity, so a phone you spoke to five minutes ago returns as a stranger and the old one lingers on the map as a node that will never reconnect. Uses expo-file-system because it is already in the build — no new native module. Falls back to a per-launch id if storage fails. Intended to become the public-key fingerprint once the vault lands so identity and key material cannot disagree.

nodes.label: enableLock (opt-in Keystore key creation)
nodes.rationale: Creating an auth-required key on a phone with nothing enrolled makes Android launch its fingerprint-enrollment flow; that must never happen as a side effect of opening the app, so the key is only ever created from an explicit user opt-in. Access control is BIOMETRY_ANY_OR_DEVICE_PASSCODE because biometry-only would shut out a phone whose owner uses a PIN.

nodes.label: unlock (prove device owner)
nodes.rationale: Not a cosmetic prompt over the UI: a secret sits in hardware-backed storage whose access policy requires device-owner authentication, so reaching the token IS the proof. The stored value itself is irrelevant.

nodes.label: hasBiometricHardware
nodes.rationale: Reports hardware presence only — says nothing about enrollment, because the only Android enrollment check is expo-local-authentication's isEnrolledAsync, which would need a native rebuild.

nodes.label: useSecureVault (unimplemented E2E vault)
nodes.rationale: Placeholder: generate/store a keypair in the hardware keychain and encrypt/decrypt payloads so mesh relays only ever see opaque ciphertext. Its stale comment claims react-native-keychain was removed, but lock.ts already imports it — the lib is back in the dev-client APK.

nodes.label: ReachMap (who can I reach right now)
nodes.rationale: Drawn with Views rather than SVG so no native dependency is added — a line is a thin View rotated about its left edge. Positions are geometry, not decoration: a direct peer sits inside the radio ring, a relayed one outside it but hanging off the peer that carries it, an unreachable one beyond everything with no line. Reading the picture must tell you the same thing as reading the hop count.
nodes.norm_label: reachmap (who can i reach right now)

nodes.label: MapNode (id/name/hops)
nodes.rationale: hops encodes three states in one field: 0 direct, >0 relayed, null unreachable — the same tri-state the mesh store writes onto threads when a peer connects or is lost.

nodes.label: MessageBubble (text + coin rows)
nodes.rationale: Money is a first-class message, not an attachment — a coin gets its own card with amount, provenance (SIGNED ON DEVICE, DIRECT vs RELAYED VIA X) and a reverted state rendered struck-through and dashed rather than removed.

nodes.label: stateLine (outgoing status text)
nodes.rationale: Renders hops+1 as "N HOPS" because hops counts relays; saying "1 HOP" about a direct hand-off would just read as noise. Outgoing only — incoming messages get a route strip instead.

nodes.label: QrCode (pure-JS run-length QR)
nodes.rationale: Pure-JS rendering avoids react-native-svg and therefore a new dev-client APK. Consecutive dark modules in a row are merged into one View, taking a 33x33 code from ~1000 views to ~150. Always dark-on-light in both themes: the code is a physical thing another phone's camera must read, and inverting it for dark mode would look consistent and scan badly.

nodes.label: useMesh hook stub (messaging/hooks)
nodes.rationale: Dead stub returning empty peers/messages; its comment still says "Transport not chosen yet" although expo-nearby-connections is integrated and the real useMesh now lives in store/mesh.ts.

nodes.label: messaging/api barrel (stale placeholder)
nodes.rationale: Exports nothing and still says "Transport TBD (expo-nearby-connections candidate)" while transport.ts in the same folder is fully implemented — consumers import the file directly, bypassing the barrel convention.

nodes.label: store barrel (stale placeholder)
nodes.rationale: Still says "Install zustand when needed" although store/mesh.ts already creates a live Zustand store; the barrel re-exports nothing.

nodes.label: useThreadSummary (on-device "catch me up")
nodes.rationale: Summarisation runs on the phone because the mesh carries ciphertext between phones — shipping plaintext to a server to summarise it would undo the thing the app is for. The model is held out of RAM via preventLoad until someone asks for a summary (~400 MB), so opening a chat stays cheap. Generation is interrupted once more than MAX_LINES lines exist because a 0.5B model will happily write an essay; a deliberate interrupt is treated as success, not failure.

nodes.label: transcript() — thread to prompt text
nodes.rationale: Slices to at most MAX_MESSAGES (40) to keep the prompt inside a small model's context window; renders coin transfers as text so non-text messages still summarise.

nodes.label: toLines() — model output sanitiser
nodes.rationale: Strips bullet characters and numbering the model added despite being told not to, then hard-caps at MAX_LINES — the prompt alone is not trusted to constrain a 0.5B model.

nodes.label: Summary SYSTEM_PROMPT
nodes.rationale: Framed as extraction rather than writing (facts, times, places, amounts, unanswered questions; no markdown), paired with temperature 0.3 and repetitionPenalty 1.15.

nodes.label: SUMMARY_MODEL provenance label
nodes.rationale: "The claim of on-device is worth nothing if the UI doesn't say which model ran and where" — the string exists purely so the sheet can prove provenance to the user.

nodes.label: useDescribeScene (placeholder)
nodes.rationale: Planned shape: feed detections to the LLM and return a natural-language scene description.

nodes.label: useReadText (OCR placeholder)
nodes.rationale: Planned shape: OCR a camera frame and return recognized text, which the feedback feature then speaks.

nodes.label: useObstacles (detection placeholder)
nodes.rationale: Planned shape: camera frames to ExecuTorch object detection, returning Detection[].

nodes.label: useProximityFeedback (placeholder)
nodes.rationale: Planned shape: nearest obstacle drives haptic pulse rate plus a spoken label.

nodes.label: useRemoteGpu (online GPU offload placeholder)
nodes.rationale: Kept opt-in and returning available:false because it breaks the 100%-offline story and sending message content off-device conflicts with the E2E-encryption goal; only content the user already sees may be summarised, with consent. Endpoint and auth are wired at the event.

nodes.label: sidequest/api — remote GPU client
nodes.rationale: Config-driven base URL plus auth token; access method is TBD until shared at the event.

nodes.label: Model service bootstrap (initExecutorch + ExpoResourceFetcher)
nodes.rationale: Registered at module scope because it must run before any model loads; the expo-file-system fetcher is what lets the ExecuTorch hooks download and cache model files.

nodes.label: VISION_MODELS group (~50 MB)
nodes.rationale: Small models for the blind-nav core (SSDLite detection + English OCR) are bundled as one group so the cheap, always-needed download is separate from the large opt-in LLM.

nodes.label: LANGUAGE_MODEL group (~400 MB, opt-in)
nodes.rationale: Qwen 2.5 0.5B quantized plus its tokenizer files, split out as opt-in because of its size.

nodes.label: downloadGroup() — pre-download to on-device cache
nodes.rationale: Fetches to cache without loading into RAM and is idempotent (cached files are skipped), so it can be re-run cheaply before an offline demo; models download once over wifi then run fully offline.

nodes.label: App (root, hand-rolled navigation)
nodes.rationale: Navigation is hand-rolled (three tabs + a one-deep stack) instead of react-navigation, because react-navigation would pull in react-native-screens + safe-area-context and force a new dev-client APK; hand-rolling keeps the whole UI hot-reloading on the build already installed. Theme follows the system by default but a header control overrides it so dark mode is always reachable on a demo phone. Unlock state is held for the life of the launch because re-prompting on every app switch would make the mesh unusable.

nodes.label: Route (one-deep modal stack state)
nodes.rationale: A nullable union of {chat,id} | {send,id}; when non-null it replaces the tab body and hides BottomNav, and the Android hardware back button pops it.

nodes.label: Avatar (hop-ringed contact circle)
nodes.rationale: The ring colour encodes hop distance so reachability reads before the name does; no route dims the whole avatar to 0.45 opacity.

nodes.label: HopChip (hop state as a pill)
nodes.rationale: Colour comes from the one signal scale; label defaults to No route / Direct / Via <relay>.

nodes.label: MeshStatus (mesh conditions strip)
nodes.rationale: The mesh states its own conditions at the top of every screen; deliberately shows no clock because the real one is two millimetres above it. The dot colour reuses the signal scale (live=direct, starting=relay, off=dim).

nodes.label: BottomNav (Reach / Wallet / Meet tabs)
nodes.rationale: Tab ids are reach|wallet|tap but the third is labelled MEET; the active tab is marked by a top border in the direct colour.

nodes.label: bottomInset (hand-measured Android nav-bar inset)
nodes.rationale: Android 15 draws edge to edge so the window already covers the nav bar and there is no gap to measure. Reading the real inset needs react-native-safe-area-context, which is native and would mean a new dev-client APK, so the code reserves 48dp (tallest 3-button nav bar) and only shrinks it if a positive gap is measurable. Marked to swap at the next rebuild.

nodes.label: RouteStrip (three-dot transit line — signature component)
nodes.rationale: Declared THE SIGNATURE COMPONENT: chat apps hide delivery behind a tick, but here the path a message took is the point, so it is drawn on screen. Flutter must match it pixel for pixel (dot sizes, segment length, hop colour) because it is the screenshot that ends up in the pitch. Animates left-to-right once for a message that just landed.

nodes.label: Display (signage typeface role)
nodes.rationale: Signage face for titles, balances, buttons and station labels.

nodes.label: Body (sentence typeface role)
nodes.rationale: Anything read as a sentence; never below 12.5pt inside a bubble.

nodes.label: Mono (mesh telemetry typeface role)
nodes.rationale: Reserved for everything the mesh reports about itself: hops, signal, times, amounts.

nodes.label: CoinMark (echocoin ring-with-E mark)
nodes.rationale: A ring with an E in it, ultramarine, money only.

nodes.label: Empty index barrels (components / hooks / screens)
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md prescribes index.ts barrels re-exporting each folder's public surface, but components/, hooks/ and screens/ barrels are still `export {}` placeholders while every consumer imports by deep path.

nodes.label: useShake (shake-to-take-it-back gesture)
nodes.rationale: Inert until the next dev-client rebuild: expo-sensors is in package.json but its JS throws from module scope when the native side is missing, and Metro evaluates the module even inside a guarded require, taking the whole app down — so the import is left commented and SHAKE_ENABLED=false. Constants (1.7g threshold, 1500ms cooldown) are kept live so they do not drift. Accessibility rule stated in-file: every action a shake triggers must also have a visible control, because a shake is undiscoverable and unusable for anyone who cannot shake a phone.

nodes.label: CatchMeUpSheet (on-device thread summary sheet)
nodes.rationale: A small model running on this phone summarises what arrived while you had no route. The model name and the NOTHING LEFT THIS DEVICE claim stay on the sheet rather than buried in settings, because that claim is the reason it runs locally at all. Summarisation auto-starts the moment the model is in RAM so there is no second button; on failure it says every message is still in the thread above.

nodes.label: ChatScreen (thread view, composer, coin cancel window)
nodes.rationale: Keeps a baseline message index so only messages arriving while the screen is open animate their route strip. Holds the unread backlog in a ref before calling markRead, because clearing the badge immediately would also remove the offer to summarise what has not been read. Shake maps to whatever the visible control does: cancel the still-held send, otherwise take back the last payment.
nodes.norm_label: chatscreen (thread view, composer, coin cancel window)

nodes.label: ReachBar (who can hear you, before you type)
nodes.rationale: Group-thread header of signal-scale pips answering who is actually reachable right now, before you type. Currently hardcoded (2 direct / 1 via Thabo / 1 out of reach) rather than derived from the mesh store.
nodes.norm_label: reachbar (who can hear you, before you type)

nodes.label: LockScreen (biometric door)
nodes.rationale: The door: nothing behind it renders until the device owner proves who they are, covering the phone-left-on-a-table case. On a phone with no fingerprint or PIN there is nothing to verify, so it offers rather than insists — turning the lock on is a deliberate tap because that is where Android may ask the user to enrol a fingerprint, and no app should spring that on someone. Respects reduce-motion for the pulse. Renders outside <Screen> so it carries its own bottom inset.

nodes.label: ModelPreloadScreen (first-run model pre-download)
nodes.rationale: Pre-downloads on-device AI models over wifi so the app runs fully offline afterward. Vision models auto-download because they are small; the LLM is opt-in because it is large. Doubles as the proof that the ExecuTorch fetch pipeline works.

nodes.label: GroupRow (per-model-group download row)
nodes.rationale: Owns its own idle/downloading/ready/error state machine and retries in place; the `auto` prop is what makes vision models fetch without a tap.

nodes.label: ReachScreen (peer map + conversation list)
nodes.rationale: Shows real mesh peers when the transport is live, and falls back to the seeded demo contact set when it is not, so a single phone still demonstrates what the screen is for. The MeshStatus strip doubles as the start/stop control; the AppBar right slot cycles the theme.

nodes.label: SendCoinScreen (echocoin keypad + queue)
nodes.rationale: After queueing it lands the user in the conversation, where the cancel window is visible; returning to the tab list would hide the only control that can stop the send. The route note states the trust claim per hop: signed here, and a relay cannot read it.

nodes.label: TapScreen (Meet a phone — pairing + key swap)
nodes.rationale: Three segments (TAP / SHOW CODE / SCAN) over one pairing flow: NFC and QR carry the same payload, so they are two doors into one feature rather than two features.
nodes.norm_label: tapscreen (meet a phone — pairing + key swap)

nodes.label: TapMode (NFC back-to-back pairing)
nodes.rationale: The fastest path when both phones have the hardware; copy points to SHOW CODE when one of them does not.

nodes.label: ShowMode (display pairing QR + fingerprint)
nodes.rationale: The fallback half you hold up; works on any phone with a camera and carries the public key and nothing else. Shows a short fingerprint to be compared out-of-band against the other screen.

nodes.label: ScanMode (camera QR reader + permission gate)
nodes.rationale: The fallback half that reads. Explains before requesting the camera that it is used only while this screen is open and only to find a pairing code, then validates the scanned string against the echo://pair scheme before offering Add contact.

nodes.label: Sonar (three staggered pairing rings)
nodes.rationale: The only looping animation in the app; it says 'still listening', which is the one thing you need while holding two phones together. Collapses to a static ring under reduce-motion.

nodes.label: echo://pair payload + fingerprint
nodes.rationale: One hardcoded demo URI (id, key, name) shared by the NFC and QR paths, plus a grouped hex fingerprint for out-of-band verification.

nodes.label: WalletScreen (balance + activity ledger)
nodes.rationale: Balance is stated as held on device and last synced with peers, not with a server. Ledger rows that travelled over a relay render the RouteStrip instead of a plain timestamp, so the path money took is visible in the money view too.

nodes.label: Hops (0 | 1 | 2 | null hop-distance type)
nodes.rationale: null encodes 'no route'; this single type is the contract every reachability visual in the UI reads.

nodes.label: Demo contacts (three-phone demo cast)
nodes.rationale: Mirrors the three-phone demo: you, Thabo (relay), Naledi (1 hop via Thabo), Lerato (direct), Sipho (no route).

nodes.label: Msg (message record with route + cancel state)
nodes.rationale: Carries hops/via per message so each bubble can draw the path it took. `pending` means held locally during the cancel window and not on the air yet; `reverted` keeps a taken-back payment row visible because money that vanishes silently is worse than money you can see was returned.
nodes.norm_label: msg (message record with route + cancel state)

nodes.label: Seeded threads (braai / thabo / naledi / sipho)
nodes.rationale: The braai group carries 11 backlog messages deliberately: enough real backlog that the on-device summary has something to work with, because a summary of four messages proves nothing. Each seeded thread demonstrates one route state (direct, 1-hop relay, queued with no route).

nodes.label: Hardcoded catch-up summary fixture
nodes.rationale: A canned WHEN/BRING/OPEN summary with a fixed model name and timing, from before the real on-device summariser existed; no module in this chunk imports it.

nodes.label: Signal scale (direct → relay → dim)
nodes.rationale: The three signal colours are ONE SCALE, not three accents: direct → relay → dim encodes hop distance (here / routed / unreachable). Every reachability visual in the app is required to read from this one scale.

nodes.label: Coin colour (money-only ultramarine)
nodes.rationale: Sits outside the signal scale because money is not a distance. Stated rule: it must never be used for signal or state, and nothing else may use it.

nodes.label: Font roles (Android system faces)
nodes.rationale: Android ships Roboto Condensed and Droid Sans Mono, so the signage role and the utility role both render for real without bundling font files — bundling would need expo-font and a new dev-client APK. Archivo Narrow + JetBrains Mono are marked to swap in at the next rebuild.

nodes.label: TOUCH_MIN (48dp minimum target)
nodes.rationale: Every control clears 48dp; nav tabs and keypad keys run larger.

nodes.label: qrcode-generator ambient module declaration
nodes.rationale: Hand-written types for an untyped JS QR library, exposing only addData/make/getModuleCount/isDark — the minimum surface needed to render a QR grid from raw modules rather than an image.
